root_cause.text: The strp_abort_strp() function in the net/strparser subsystem failed to release the partially assembled socket buffer stored in strp->skb_head when aborting the stream parser, causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states "That skb is not released in strp_abort_strp()", and the patch diff shows the addition of kfree_skb(strp->skb_head) within the strp_abort_strp() function to fix this omission.

intent_record.intent_summary: Prevent memory leaks and stale state by releasing pending SKBs and resetting parser fields during abort.
intent_record.what: Added conditional logic to free strp->skb_head if non-NULL, explicitly set strp->skb_nextp to NULL, and reset strp->need_bytes to 0.
intent_record.how: Ensures pending socket buffer data is released and parser state variables are cleared during the abort sequence to prevent memory leaks and dangling references.

grouping_result.intent: Prevent memory leaks and stale state by releasing pending SKBs and resetting parser fields during abort.

relevance_review.reason: The group's intent to release pending SKBs and reset fields during abort directly addresses the root cause of the memory leak caused by failing to release strp->skb_head in strp_abort_strp().
